sources.note: No prosodic (stress/rhythm) features coded for Manem.

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org (Greenhill), language page 'Manem' (141 lexical items from Voorhoeve 1971, 1975).
sources.note: Lexical data only; transcriptions carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid Manem (mane1266): MED = 'wordlist or less' (Stokhof 1983 Holle lists; Voorhoeve 1971; Galis 1955; Cowan 1952); local Glottolog 5.1 sources.bib: 14 Manem-tagged entries, none of hhtype grammar / grammar_sketch / phonology.
sources.note: n/a (bibliographic database; confirms no grammar or phonology of Manem is registered).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 345-460. [Manem: sec. 2.6.2.2.11.2.1.2, p. 416]
sources.note: Nothing. The half-page Manem note lists consonants (like Waris but no velar fricative, r instead of l), vowels i e a o u ə (possibly ü ö), verb/noun affix categories, pronouns, SOV order; no prosody. (The same chapter does give stress remarks for other, non-Border languages, so the silence is specific to Manem/Waris.)

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31). Canberra: ANU. [Manem = entry 104; wordlist 104]
sources.note: Nothing language-specific; the wordlist transcription conventions state 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.' Entry 104 gives villages (Wembi, Uskwar, Kibae, Yeti, Skofro, Skotiaho, Kriku), ~400 speakers, sources Galis 1955, Cowan 1957b, Voorhoeve 1971, Laycock 1973.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. Dutton et al., Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU. [Manem pp. 60-64 + appendix wordlist]
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.3.3 'Phonology' (pp. 62-64) gives a tentative segment inventory for Awji, Taikat, Manem, Waris: for Manem prenasalised voiced stops, /ŋ/ with allophones [gŋ]~[ŋ] and innovating final [r], vowels i e a o u ə (+ provisional ü ö), consonant clusters incl. word-final CC; no mention of stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Smits, Leo & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1994. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya languages, B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages, Part I (Irian Jaya Source Materials No. 9, Series B No. 3). Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS. 288 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Contains Anceaux's Manem (Wembi/Skofro) wordlists; Anceaux-collection transcriptions sometimes mark stress with an acute, which would be the only phonetic stress evidence for Manem even without a prose rule.

sources.citation: Cowan, H. K. J. 1952. De austronesisch-papoea'se taalgrens in de onderafdeling Hollandia (Nieuw Guinea). Tijdschrift Nieuw-Guinea 13: 133-143, 160-177, 201-206 (and Cowan 1957b, cited by Voorhoeve for Manem data).

sources.note: Earliest first-hand Wembi/Skofro (= Manem) material; Cowan occasionally comments on accent in his North-Papuan comparisons; low probability of a Manem-specific stress remark but not checked.
